parts.name: preparation
parts.title: Preparation
parts.text:
1. PREPARATION
Run `vw visuals prepare` once the first cut is approved (nothing is made or paid). It writes the package under work/visuals/, one file per section (prompt.md, gaps.json, intended-visuals.json, brief.json, world-1.json and on with 25 clips each, schema.json, generators.json), and the image prompt library per step under work/visuals/library/ (section 6, in part-later.md); read a file whole, never by line offsets. Read prompt.md and gaps.json first, and claims.json (the figures the narration rests on, and whether the operator had them checked: a picture or graphic shows the same figure, and a checked one is not searched again), the world files when you plan the scenes. Tell the operator (never ask) its one line on the footage's look, measured from the clips; their correction, said in the chat (`vw visuals footage`), wins. Then settle and record the treatment (section 2, part-treatment.md), before any plan or picture.

parts.name: treatment
parts.title: Treatment
parts.text:
2. TREATMENT
The Direction comes first (refused without), the central creative choice, written as `direction_parts`, six short parts in this order, two or three sentences each: `idea`, the film's one idea in one sentence (if it cannot be said in one, the idea is not clear yet); `purpose`, who the film is for and what it must do, taken from the brief (where the Direction departs from the brief, say so there); `viewpoint`, whose story it is: One viewpoint, held for the whole film; `feel`, what the viewer should feel, tied to concrete choices of pace, light and movement ("cinematic" or "immersive" alone is not a tone); `shape`, the film from its opening to its end in beats: one beat for each turn in what the viewer learns, as many as the film's length needs (about three in a one-minute film); `pictures`, what real footage, generated scenes and graphics each do and why, how each follows from the idea, and what the film will not do. Be specific and committed ("short scenes of one person doing one thing", not "a mix of techniques"). The server joins the parts into `direction` under their headings, refuses a part over its length (160, 300, 200, 300, 400 and 500 characters) and shows the operator a part not given as not given. When the operator asks for a different direction, keep the first, write a second in `direction_alternative` (its six parts, `answers_brief`, `risk`) that differs in viewpoint or approach, not in wording, and give each of the two how it answers the brief and what it risks (the first's in `direction_answers_brief` and `direction_risk`); the operator takes one; the server places the accepted Direction at the head of the plan's `foundation.treatment`. A palette or "documentary mix" alone is not a direction. Choose the picture from the film's purpose, audience and script before you think about how it is made: the effort, cost or convenience of a route never chooses the medium. Choose from the narration alone: the script's visual notes are not used and not cited. Choose from what the sentence tells the viewer, not from a noun in it, and show the real, tangible thing before a general view. For anything a camera could film, first ask who is doing what, and write the picture as a person doing one action that shows the meaning; the order of the ways for a scene is real footage that shows it; else AI video; else a still, with the reason. Use a symbol only when it reads at a glance; otherwise be literal. Bring the film's key pictures back (the same person, place or object). A still moves slowly; one the viewer must read (a document, a page, a sign) is held steady, your call. Words on the picture: in an advertisement, product or social film, key words, three words or fewer at a time; in a documentary or explainer, none beyond a diagram's labels (the subtitles carry the words). In a documentary or a client story, people, purposeful work and the material changing under their hands carry the film; a realistic representative scene is a legitimate picture when the footage lacks one, provided it does not pretend to be the client's own site, people or measured result. There is no quota of AI video, footage or graphics: a technical record may lean on graphics, a human story on scenes; say in the direction which the film is and why. With no footage, the direction also holds the film's one look (colours, contrast, light), approved once, read wherever a plan rule reads the footage beside a gap.
Read the whole first cut, including the retained footage before, between and after the gaps. Plan the missing passages in film order as one progression: what the audience already knows, what each adds, changes of pace, recurring visual ideas, how each enters from and exits into the neighbouring real pictures. Use a diagram, chart or illustrated graphic when the meaning is invisible to a camera or must be read precisely: the inside of something (a cross-section, a cavity, a hidden layer); a flow, force, heat or load path; a number, comparison or proportion the narration rests on; a sequence where the order matters; scale; or before and after. Use a scene (footage, or AI video or still of people and places) for people, places, materials, textures, effort, feeling and results, anything a camera could have filmed with more time. Build the film's graphics as one visual language: one recurring diagram that develops across the film reads better than many unrelated drawings. Vary the pictures: mix the shots of a gap longer than one shot (footage, an AI scene, a labelled scene, a graphic); two graphics in a row only when each passes the test above, the second's `warning_answers` saying why (warned, as is a gap of graphics only). A footage clip, or a specific thing the footage shows (one building, one machine), is named at one gap only; a second gap that wants it says why in its line, or takes another. The gap that opens the film (if one does) opens on the subject, framed wide enough to see where, never an empty view of the place; a close-up comes after a wider view. Propose in the treatment the look of a gap with no real footage beside it (palette, contrast, saturation, light; by default the look the film's category and the Direction call for: on a documentary-explainer film muted and true to life; with no footage, the direction's look), approved with it.
The treatment, in out/visual-treatment.json, has one entry per gap: `gap_id`; the words under it; `picture` in one line; `routes`; `seconds`, one number, the gap's total (a video gap's segments carry theirs inside `shots`, never a list in `seconds`); `images`, a whole number for the gap (a count, never a list: one still per AI video shot); an AI video shot may be any kind of shot, with or without a person (section B); a person in it does one action, hand work is close and in the right hand, and every transfer is named and close; a line that rests on a rule on trial says so; `depicts`, one line per graphic, approved before anything is drawn; `frozen_seconds` held still (usually 0); and `shots` with each `route` and `seconds`, its `picture`, `fits_why` (why the picture fits the words and what the viewer understands better with it) and `way_why` (why it is made this way: could a real clip do it, why a diagram and not a photo, why a still and not a video), one or two sentences each, shown to the operator with the shot; a gap of one way with no `shots` carries the two reasons on its line. End with your reasons; the server refuses a gap missing or twice or a field out of form, and adds per route the counts and seconds, the cost against the cap and the frozen share against its 10 % limit.
Write the Direction alone first: send a draft that holds only the Direction (`vw visuals treatment --file out/visual-treatment.json`, no `gaps` in it), then `vw visuals page`: on a page the operator chooses the film's motion style (asked once; the page shows every style and the recommended one with its reason) and answers the Direction; nothing is recorded until they say done in the chat. Write no gap line before the Direction is accepted. Then write every gap line from the accepted Direction, send the whole treatment with the Direction unchanged, and `vw visuals page` again for the gap lines. Do what its `how` says, in order: publish the page once by its file, write each round to it from the round file (type none of it), give the operator the link, and when they say done read their answers and record them with `vw visuals page --record`. Where the page cannot be shown, say so once and use `vw visuals next`: the server asks the Direction alone, as one question (recorded with `vw visuals decide`), then hands the operator the gap lines on one card, and you record the card with `vw visuals card` (section E; one line at a time with `vw visuals decide` where the card cannot be shown either). There is no yes to the whole. Revise only a line sent back and send the draft again; unchanged accepted lines stay accepted, one your revision changed (a shared route, the totals) returns to "to accept". Recorded when every line is accepted, the treatment comes before any plan or picture; the plan is checked against it. Settle the direction in conversation before planning, and a material change as a decision before shots; never quietly rewrite an accepted foundation: a changed direction revises the treatment, sequence, affected world rules and scenes together, never a new rule beside shots that contradict it.

parts.name: plan
parts.title: The detailed plan
parts.text:
3. THE DETAILED PLAN
Order of work, in three steps, to the recorded treatment: foundation, elements, gaps (scenes, shots, states for animation shots, beats). You write the shared parts in out/plan-base.json: foundation, elements (the film's techniques among them, kind technique, named once here from the treatment and the footage; a beat verb outside them is warned, never refused), graphic style, sequence_overview, `gaps` (in order); then the missing facts (section A), their answers written into plan-base.json. Before the first check, read your own part once: every person has a `description` that gives their age, build, hair and face, so that no two people read alike (the check names every pair that does, `people_alike`: fix them all at once; the reference round refuses them); a material has its unit sizes or its amount; a place shown has two `signs_of_use` or `staged_clean`; no size is left `proposed`; `world` holds the place, the period and what is normally there, and `exclusions` what the period forbids. Then helpers (the `vw-plan-gaps` helper, a few gaps each; start with three or four) write the gaps at once from out/plan-base.json, the package, the recorded treatment and their neighbours (pictures before and after, the people's last state), never another helper's gaps, one file each in out/plan-gaps/ (a gap, or {"gaps": [...]}), things not among the elements in `new_elements` (id and name), never invented; a short film you may write alone. `vw visuals plan-join --base out/plan-base.json --gaps out/plan-gaps/` writes out/visual-plan.json (film order, new things merged by name; a missing or doubled gap is refused; it names the new things still to complete). When a helper's report does not arrive, its file under out/plan-gaps/ (read by its full path) is the proof it finished: never relaunch a helper whose file exists. `vw visuals check --file out/visual-plan.json` until valid: it lists every shot's first fault and the plan-wide faults together (a way the treatment did not name among them); fix them all before sending again; a clean check means the proposal is taken (it checks across gaps and prints routes, graphic seconds, images and cost against the cap); fix what it names in the gap file (its helper for a judgement, you for a field or a spelling) or, for a shared part, in out/plan-base.json; join again, check again, before a proposal and after one: after a proposal the join carries your changes onto the server's plan and keeps what was corrected there. A hand edit of out/visual-plan.json is never overwritten: the join says what to do (`--rebuild` drops the hand edits). Answer each warning in the shot's `warning_answers` ({kind, answer}), never in the purpose, or change the plan; the operator reads the plain warnings on the plan page, above each gap's shots; never tell them the technical ones. Before proposing, review each passage's meaning and treatment fit, every subject's beats, layout and scale against the landmarks, identity against the references, continuity with the neighbours and across shots, every shot's route and length against its generator, every sequence's states, and exact placement timing. `vw visuals propose --file out/visual-plan.json` (refused before the recorded treatment or when a gap's route departs from it; the server places the accepted Direction at the head of `foundation.treatment`: write only your own text there, or leave it out); then `vw visuals page`: the operator answers the whole plan on the page in one visit (a change of the shared rules, a gap offered two ways with each way's shots, every gap's shots as a table), and nothing is recorded until they say done in the chat. Do what its `how` says, then `vw visuals page --record`; change what they sent back, propose again, and `vw visuals page` again. Where the page cannot be shown, say so once and use `vw visuals next`: the server asks an offered choice first, as buttons (or, with the operator's answer, `vw visuals select --gap G --choice C`), then hands the operator the gaps on one card, and you record the card with `vw visuals card` (section E; one gap at a time with `vw visuals decide` where the card cannot be shown either); never `accept --gaps all`. A plan proposed again keeps every acceptance it did not touch. When the new version changes only the part every gap shares (the foundation, the sequence rules), the server asks the operator ONE question for all the gaps whose own shots are unchanged, and lists what changed; a gap whose own shots changed is asked by itself, with what changed. Never ask those gaps one by one, never say yourself what changed or that a gap is unchanged: show what the server hands out. Change the foundation or a sequence rule only when the change asked for needs it, and say so before you propose. Before any picture, read every gap's words in `vw visuals status`: a change asked for, or a gap sent back, is a revision (Revise, or `vw visuals revise --gap G --notes "…" --quote "…"`): revise its treatment entry and plan (one helper for one gap), propose again for fresh acceptance and generate nothing for it until then; unchanged gaps stay accepted.
The foundation, a practical casting and production-design brief, has one topic per rule (id, statement, scope, source) in separate categories: world (place, period, people and their work, wardrobe, environment, materials, tools, signage, language, the process, and what is normally there; short positive statements, only what this film needs, no invented region or dress); exclusions (detectable consequences of the direction, each naming the decision it protects, and what the period forbids; no generic negatives, no ban on a medium because one option was rejected); specifications; production_constraints (narration and first cut preserved); editing_constraints (rejected pictures, their intervals); appearance (style, colour, lighting; texture, sharp or soft, from the measured footage character, the operator's correction winning; with no footage, the direction's look). Layouts live in scenes, identities in elements, temporal rules in sequence_rules; the foundation alone should let another director work. Each statement is one of three kinds: a requirement or observed fact with its source (brief, script, the operator's words, a clip finding), applied no wider than the evidence; a creative choice marked Proposed, with its film-specific reason; a consequential unknown, asked in open_questions and `vw visuals ask`, when a choice would assert real geography, identity, culture or performance the sources do not establish. Never fill an unknown with a stereotype or an inferred nationality, nor defer every casting and environment decision: propose the shared direction now, defer exact identities and props. sequence_overview first: what each gap adds to the treatment's progression. An ordinary gap has one proposal in gap.scenes (treatment_fit: its part in the sequence); two choices (each with scenes, a recommended_choice, a plain decision_reason; other shapes refused) only for a real ambiguity, a production constraint or the operator's request; the order of preference holds for each way: real footage that shows it, else AI video, else a still. A plain or studio background only when the treatment allows it (`studio_background`, with the reason); objects shown where made, kept or used, not alone.
Meaning. Give each passage its key meaning, emotional weight and a concrete method (evidence, process, a person's experience, or another justified approach). An abstract thought, feeling or statistic is valid narration: never rewrite it for a camera or fabricate documentary evidence (a graphic may explain a statistic); never invent facts, people, claims, scale or physical mechanisms. Per shot: `claims` and `descriptors`, never shown as their opposite (warned when missing on a shot with narration); `evidence` when it carries a claim (a test, a table, or the result in a scene, never an unrelated picture; warned when missing); `claim`, visible (footage first; warned on a graphic) or invisible; `fact_ids` into `visual_facts` (how a material, process or setting really looks and is done; source and status: confirmed, observed, unknown; warned when missing on a shot of a material or process); `carries_over` for a process's next step (one process, one place, light and crew; "on top of that" or "once" is no process); `message`, with `adds` (a number, a cause, a consequence) when it repeats, or the two become one shot. An MCU, CU or ECU resting on an unknown fact is refused: frame wider or ask the operator.
Elements. Derive them from the planned shots (secondary subjects, named background people, props), each exact (the same individual, object or place throughout) or representative, with its views. Anything specific to the client the footage shows (a pattern, a product, a tool, a uniform) is its own exact object element, its footage frames as views and its description once in the world rules as exact text; until its golden picture exists, its pictures send one of those frames as a parent, never words alone. A thing whose fact or size cites the footage (a clip or its frame; a maker's "door frame" is not footage) is `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame before any picture, measured first (`vw visuals measure`, status measured) when its size is unknown: warned in the plan, refused at the picture. Materials and processes the film relies on are elements (kind material, process), as are tools in a holding or props list (object) and techniques a beat names as its working action (technique: kneading, soldering, welding; not a gesture or a tool's name: "points at the screen", "picks up the drill"), all in the reference round; a technique is `identity: representative` (the trade's usual way) unless its fact or size cites the footage (the client's own technique, as filmed): then `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame, like any thing the footage shows; a missing technique is refused (`status.needed_elements`). Every person, object and animal has its real `size` (client material, `measure` on footage frames, a maker's sheet; else unknown, never invented; warned when missing; a generic, standardised thing's size may be proposed from a named standard or maker figure, status `proposed`, source "recalled: <standard>, to confirm", put to the operator in the missing-facts list beside its alternatives and the footage measure, and recorded on their word as confirmed, source "the operator confirmed <standard>": it may shape the drawing, never a number written on screen (that needs the script, the client's document or a web check); a client's own thing is never proposed from recall), a material laid as repeating units (tiles, planks, pavers) its unit sizes in its `material_spec`; a liquid or a loose material (water, sand, paint) carries none: its `requirements` say how much is used or how much of the surface it covers, and the shot shows it; a claim in `claims` about the subject's own size, amount or scale is refused without a size value and `compare_to` (another element in frame: a person first; with no person, a thing whose size is generally fixed, such as a door, a chair or a hand tool); the server puts the size sentence into the prompt of the still and of the AI video's starting picture; a size word in `descriptors` or a beat describes and is not checked, except on a graphic or drawn shot or for light, less, fewer or short not about size. Refused without: a person's `description`, the fixed layer (face, build, hair), which never changes; each scene's `outfit` per person shown (garments and colours only; a framing note goes in the shot's `focus`, a question in `open_questions`). A person keeps the same clothes within one continuous time. When the time changes (later the same day, another day, another season, years later) the clothes may change: the scene's `outfit` then names the garment types as well as the colours, and `time_jump` says what changed in time, from the script or the scene's own time (refused without). Two different people in one scene are not dressed in the same colours unless a uniform is the point. Nothing in the frame vanishes: everything in the shot at its start is accounted for at its end, still there at a stated place (a subject's `end`, a prop's end) or gone by a stated action of someone; anything that moves or is moved is a named subject or prop of the shot, the container that brings a thing included (warned as container_unnamed). `speaker: true` marks a real, named person and nothing more. Each person is one of two kinds. Own likeness: the operator gives the person's photo and says, in their own words, that they have the person's permission (`vw visuals likeness --element E --quote "<their words>"`, then `vw visuals own --element E --file <photo>`); the sheet is made from the photo. Both commands need a proposed plan: record the permission and give the photo after the plan is proposed; the operator's line about a stand-in goes away once the permission is recorded. A stand-in: no photo; the person is made from the description. If the picture service refuses the photo, ask the operator for another photo or make the person a stand-in (`vw visuals likeness --element E --stand-in --quote "…"`). The server tells the operator in one plain line when a real, named person is shown as a stand-in. A take has no sound: a person can be shown, not made to speak in time with the voice.
Scenes and life. A scene is one setting, time and purpose; beats are the smallest visible actions. `activity_level` (quiet, normal or busy) from the narration and the brief; a normal or busy scene shows the implied life (who else does what) and the things in use around them (warned). Up to ten people are named in the background of a scene, each an element with their own description and beats; beyond ten, each further person is described one by one in a `groups` entry with `mode: different` (one trait per head). `mode: varied` is retired. Never write "crowd", or a word that suggests one, in anything that goes to a picture. Every named person gets a character sheet in the reference round. This holds for stills as well as AI video. Everything visible that acts (person, animal or object) has beats; a still one holds, with `hold_reason`, unchanged. A scene with a video shot has its ambient line: one line on what moves around the action (leaves in the breeze, dust or smoke in the air, people at work behind), from the setting and the neighbouring footage, or 'still' (warned without; the server writes it into every take and the take check asks for it); every scene its `light` once (a scene of graphics only (diagrams, sequences, drawn) has none; the sources against the landmarks, the main one, hard or soft, colour, strength; warned without; the check measures each picture's light and colour against the footage beside it and marks a large jump) and its air (dust, smoke, haze, steam or clean), matched to the footage beside the gap (with no footage, the direction's look) and named word for word in the prompt (soft overcast light, muted greens). Props fit the work and the region (a kettle in a kitchen), never what the setting forbids (no smoking, flame or spark near fuel, gas or chemicals) or an unsafe practice shown as right. Ask of the world: for this place and this time, what would a viewer expect to see that the script does not name? Write it once in `world`, as exact kinds (for example overhead wires on poles along a road, a street dog of the region, house sparrows), and write once in `exclusions` what the period forbids (a film set in 1850: nothing electric, no plastic, no motor vehicle). Use it lightly: a picture takes at most one or two of these, and not every shot has one. A living extra is an element of kind `animal`, named by its exact kind with its `size`, so it stays the same size; it gets no reference sheet. A shot shows one kind of animal. The same living extra is not in two shots in a row unless it carries on from the shot before. Fixed things (poles, wires, signs, street furniture) are landmarks of the place and stay where they are in every picture of it. This applies to stills and to the starting picture of an AI video; plan no moving animal in an AI video. People leave traces where they work or live (tools left out, offcuts, spills, footprints; a worn chair, cups on a desk): a place shown needs `signs_of_use` (two or more, each at one of its landmarks; refused without) unless the treatment approves it clean (a new empty room, a showroom, a product studio), the reason in `staged_clean`. In a video shot or a still, several of a kind in one frame (counted above one, or a framing word such as people, children, cows, unless negated: "no people yet") need a `groups` entry, `same` (with the reason) or `different` (one trait per head); refused otherwise.
Positions, states and beats. Lay out each scene with named landmarks (the doorway, the table, the near wall), room positions apart from the screen sides; a moving subject heads for something in frame or coming into view. Each subject: a role, screen position, start and end states, facing, pose, held objects and progress; an acting one ordered timed beats (start and end, target, path, contact, visible result). Its first beat starts exactly in the subject's `start` state and its last beat ends exactly in its `end` state, field for field (position, facing, pose, holding, progress, objects, gaze), and each beat starts in the previous beat's end (refused otherwise, naming the shot, the subject, the beat and the fields that differ). Refused: a position without landmark, `amount` and `unit`; `facing` not a heading; `objects` without `count` and `place`; a held tool without `props`; an object count that changes without its `changes` entry; a carriable thing in `fixed`; a beat without `done` or with a free-word target (a landmark or an element id of the shot; describe it in path and result); a person's state without `gaze` (its target may be `camera`) unless `face_in_frame` is false; a video shot whose `fixed` is not three landmark ids (all when fewer; at MCU, CU or ECU only those in frame, none allowed); a beat shorter than its `min_s` (setting one cup down, about 2 s) or actions that overrun the shot. Warned: a missing `min_s`; an acting video shot without `changes` (none for ambient-only shots); a state changed between shots without a note (a cut never teleports a person or resets work). The server writes the rule lines from these fields (two signs of use per shot, or 'clean and unused, as planned') and checks every picture and take against them; on a film whose reference round is of the new kind a background figure repeated from another picture of the scene is a line of Claude's check; before, `status.figure_repeats` names repeated background figures. `boundary_continuity` (required): how the first and last shot continue the neighbours on both sides, footage or planned (at the film's start or end, the one side).
Timing and movement. Narration is timed per gap (gaps.json `timing`: sentences in seconds, words in frames; context.timing adds the sentences either side). Cut in a pause, never inside a word; a shot's `narration` is the words it covers, its picture starting on or just before them, a title or label on its word (warned otherwise). Shots run two to eight seconds as a rule, never mechanically equal; AI video 1 to 15 s on screen (a take is made at 3 s or more and trimmed; under 1 s use a picture; over 15 s refused; an action of 9 s or more is better as two shots cut on the action); a picture or a drawing may be a second or two. Real footage in a gap is a footage shot (`visual_type: footage`, `vw visuals clip`), under the timing, crop, reuse and no-repeat rules only, not those for generated pictures (the 15 s limit and `information_progression` among them). Every still and graphic state moves 5 % (`motion`, from the composition); a graphic or a text picture only push_in or none; `none` needs `motion_reason` (refused otherwise). Warned: a moving still over 4 s, a frozen one over 3 s, a graphic state over 5 s, one graphic over 4 s (not a title or text card: a build of 2 to 4 states or a drawn animation), a label or one number under three seconds, a run of graphics over 8 s (a building diagram fits within; break it with a camera shot). Fill a longer stretch with several stills, a clip stretch (`vw visuals clip --shot S --clip C --at <in seconds>`) or a take. Each shot has a size (EWS, WS, MWS, MS, MCU, CU, ECU) and a camera_reason (eye level honest, low powerful, high vulnerable, a slow push draws in; no angle has one fixed meaning; warned when missing, footage excepted). A scene's first camera shot is EWS, WS or MWS. Never frame a third shot in a row at one size. Frame MCU or closer only after its subject was seen at MS or wider in this scene or the one just before. When the footage beside the gap already showed the place, set `continues_footage: true`; when the gap before showed it, or a reveal is meant, write `size_reason`. A shot about a look or an expression is framed MCU or closer with the face in frame, and the person's face picture is among its references. A miss comes back to you as a technical warning to fix; the operator is not told. A clip needing more than 1.35× to fill the frame keeps bars (warned): crop it to the frame's shape (`vw visuals clip … --crop x,y,w,h`) or choose another. Name every join: `transition_in` on every shot (`transition_out` on a gap's last shot only): cut, dissolve or match; a dissolve or a match with `transition_reason`; refused without. The same person may appear as often as the film needs. The same person in the same place, in the same clothes and at the same size, is not shown twice: the second showing differs in angle, distance or moment (`return_of`, `differs_by`), the earlier picture only as identity reference. When the script itself stays in one place (a workplace), the place may stay and the framing changes. The identical picture is never used in two shots, and a frozen frame of a clip playing elsewhere never shows. A clip shown again (first cut or here) is a reuse: give the reason and the reimagined shot you considered, `vw visuals clip|still … --reuse "<reason>" --considered "<the reimagined shot and why it adds nothing>" --crop x,y,w,h`. A reuse that passes the checks is kept: another stretch of the clip, within its safe enlargement, at least 60 s from the other showing, or a quarter of the film when that is shorter. It does not wait for the operator; `vw visuals reuse` is retired. Warned, for you to fix: the frozen share, pictures that look alike.
Graphics. A graphic that builds or reveals is one animation shot of two to four states, each adding something and holding at least three seconds, together filling the shot (refused otherwise); an unchanging one is a diagram shot, one still. A drawn shot is named at plan time by `visual_type: drawn` alone (no `scene_svg` yet); its scene is drawn, uploaded and named after the picture search (section 9, in part-later.md). A drawn shot carries one camera flow, `camera_flow`, chosen by what the explanation is doing: naming parts, comparing two things, a quantity (a chart, heaps, counts), a change of state, a flow (load, heat, water) or a title or text: `fixed` (a comparison and a quantity always: a camera move changes how big things look); whole to part: `step_closer`; part to whole: `pull_back`; longer than the frame, or a process in a line: `pan_along` (a flow only when its path leaves the frame); a map: `step_closer` or `pan_along`; parts named one after another, closer each time: `follow` (at most three steps); one idea held through a long sentence, with no label near the edge: `slow_push_in`. One camera flow per shot; fixed when in doubt (no field is fixed). A flow the film's motion style does not allow is warned. A drawn shot of a HyperFrames film carries its texts and cues in the plan, with the plan, before the first brief: `scene_motion: {labels, cues}` (labels: every text the viewer reads, word for word, never the corner note, which is the server's; cues `{selector: "#id", word or at_s}`; no sha256: the server binds the project that passes its fact check). A drawing with no text at all has `labels: []`. `vw motion brief` is refused while a drawn shot that carries text has none. The corner note and a logo picture are not text the shot carries: a shot whose only text they are has `carries_text: false`. The plan check names a drawn shot that carries text and lists no labels (`labels_missing`), and a logo or a brand picture whose file was not given (`supplied_missing`: ask the operator for the file with the plan; it goes in in/brand/). Labels in words the plan already holds, and `carries_text: false` on such a shot, ask the operator nothing; a label in new words is asked with its gap. `graphic_kind`: `diagram`, `chart`, `map`, `title` or `text` (a card checked only for its words, spelling and size); in a documentary or an explaining film a card of words is warned and the operator is told: show the thing, and let the voice say the words. Each state names the claims and words it shows (`what_appears`, `words`; what none names is checked on the last) and starts on its `words`. `depicts`: the film's subject in its own form; an alternative (the conventional way, a competitor's) only as a labelled contrast the narration calls for. Labels: short complete phrases ("25 % less material", not "↓ 25 %"), numbers with units, leader lines ending on their part, at least 4 % of the frame height (titles 6 %), readable on a phone, in the answer's exact text (section B). Each claim spoken over a graphic is in `claims` (a must line) or `claims_left_out` with the reason; a build has a state per claim (warned); a state like the one before is refused; the assembly film is checked for every planned state. One graphic style per film (foundation.graphic_style: palette from the client card, line weight, labels, background, frame fill), made first as a style sheet when the plan has a graphic in steps (`vw visuals image --element _STYLE --kind style --answer …`; a film whose graphics are all drawn has none), approved, in the --parents of every graphic's first (or only) picture, later states inheriting it; every picture and take carries its --answer; warned: missing claims, depicts, style, spec approval or answers.
Drawing specs. A drawing of a real object is drawn to the convention of its field (a plan, a section or an elevation; dimension lines with units) and to scale. If it is not to scale, or any size in it is unknown, it carries the words "not to scale" (`illustrative: true`, the words in its `label`) and shows no figure for the unknown size. A size the narration states is always shown as stated. It has a `drawing_spec` (warned without; an idea graphic with no real object or figure, such as heat leaving a house, needs none): parts, relationships, each size with status (confirmed: the client's source; measured; unknown) and source, and `view` with `view_reason` (give both; a section defaults to cutaway), checked on the drawing. Research every size before the spec is shown, in this order: the client's material; the footage, measured (`vw visuals measure --refs F1 F2 --question "<what to measure>"` on approved footage frames, each number keeping its clip and time; paid: announce, never ask); a standard or maker's sheet on the web, with URL and figure (one warning and one yes cover every web figure of the run); an approved reference picture for a shape numbers cannot hold. Each value carries its source and status, a spec of a real object its proportions (a box about 3 : 2 : 1; a drawing spec is warned without them, a material spec refused). Refused: an unknown with a value, a figure the shot's narration or claims state marked unknown (it is confirmed from the script), an illustrative drawing not labelled "illustrative, not to scale" (no numbers, no free proportions). A size may still wait for its research (paid measures and web figures come after the picture search): an `unknown` size that does not say in `tried` what was tried, and `illustrative: true` missing when a size is unknown, are warned in the plan (`spec_unresearched`) and refused when the spec is approved; `status.illustrative` warns above one in four. The SVG scene labels known sizes with units. The operator never types a size: after the plan is accepted they approve the sizes, materials and graphic specs on the page (`vw visuals page`, one visit, then `vw visuals page --record`); in the chat, one at a time (`vw visuals next`), only where the page cannot be shown. A correction they send is in `spec_corrections`: fold into out/visual-plan.json (`vw visuals plan`), propose again (approval refused until then), then `vw visuals page` again; a correction said in the chat: `vw visuals spec --shot S --notes "…"`.

parts.name: picture-search
parts.title: The picture search
parts.text:
4. THE PICTURE SEARCH
The references are one round for every element at once (people, objects, places, the materials and processes the film relies on), never one element at a time. Find each thing in the footage first: `vw visuals digest` writes what every clip shows, part by part with seconds (work/visuals/digest/index.json, then the clips files it names), and the things with the frame rule and the limits (work/visuals/refs/things.json); then do what its answer says. With more than five things start `vw-reference-finder` helpers, about five things each, up to six at a time, each given a group name, its thing ids, the run folder's path and the tool's command line; with five or fewer do the same yourself. For each thing: name the likely moments from the digest, take small trial frames (`vw visuals trial --file`, rows {element, clip, at}), read every frame, and record what was seen (`vw visuals look --file`: {by, things: [{element, clips, note, looks: [{trial, view, verdict, seen, keep, closest, face, child}]}]}; verdict pass, weak or fail; on a person's frame `face` says whether it shows their face and `child` whether they are a child, as seen, never guessed from words): `keep` on the best frame of each of the thing's views, `closest` on the nearest frame where none can be kept, `not_searched` with the reason where no search was possible. A trial frame is not a reference. The server decides each thing's result, refuses a look on a frame that was not fetched, and names the things still to search. On a run with no digest its answer says so: `vw visuals elements` then names the likely clips by words (work/visuals/elements.json), every frame still needs its look, and the operator is told the footage was searched by words only. The rule for a good frame is the server's and travels in things.json: judge every frame by it and by no rule of your own. A frame becomes a footage picture only through its look: the server cuts a kept frame at full size, source and time kept, and refuses, when the round is sent, a footage picture with no recorded look and a thing with no search record. Footage left out of the edit is searched too (not the operator's explicit exclusions). A footage frame of a person serves your description; it goes to the picture AI only with the person's recorded permission (own likeness, part-plan.md; a footage frame may still be a video take's start image). Where a kept frame shows a person's face, step 1 asks the operator one thing: whether they have that person's permission (a parent's or guardian's for a child). With it the kept frames go to the set, the best face frame first; without it a stand-in is made from the description, who will differ from the person in the clips. Where the person in the footage is not the film's character, give that row no frames (`frames: []`): nothing is asked then.
A thing whose construction, pattern or mechanism must be right in a picture, or which a picture AI is unlikely to know, is drawn before the round: load the `vw:drawing` skill; a `vw-drawing` helper writes its drawing set as data (its facts, each with its source or marked assumed; its pieces in real sizes; its views) and sends it, `vw drawing set --element E --file work/drawing/E/set.json` (the server draws every view and refuses a faulty set in plain words). The operator approves the reference drawings on the page (`vw visuals page`, which also sends the pictures as it says): the labelled sheets, small and large on a click, with the sources and the assumed sizes, and they answer Yes or Correct it; in the chat, one at a time (`vw visuals next`), only where the page cannot be shown. Approved drawings go with that thing's set by themselves, with the words that explain them and its facts. Where the footage and the plan's sizes disagree, draw from the footage and tell the operator in one line. A loose or living thing gets a form sheet; a person never gets a drawing set. A drawing set is a reference for the picture AI; it is not the drawing spec of a drawn graphic.
Then the round, once every thing is searched and any drawing set is approved: write out/reference-round.json, one row per element, every person a picture is made of included and none for an animal: element_id; `rec`, your proposal (`footage`: use its footage picture; `clean`: a clean set made from it; `set`: have a set made; `no_set`: its words carry it; `leave`: no reference needed); `reason`, one line the operator reads, which names no cost and no cost word (never "free" or "paid"); `first` on up to three rows of different kinds, the sets made first; and `prompt` only for what the plan does not say. For a place, also `things`: the ids of the film's own objects and materials that are fixed parts of it or always stand in it in the film (a tiled roof's tile, a room's window shutter), most important first, never a tool or a prop that only passes through a shot and never a person, [] when there are none, and `things_reason`, one plain line: a place is made only after their sets are approved, with their pictures. When the server asks for a place's list later, `vw visuals round --things` shows what to read and takes the file. Where the plan's thing and the footage differ (the footage shows a trial piece on the ground, the plan the finished thing in its place), write in `prompt` what to take from the footage and what from the plan: the request ranks these words above the film's pictures, your check judges by them, and the operator reads them on the line. For a way of working propose `leave` unless a still picture (not an AI video) shows the action, and say so in the reason: on the video route nothing reads its set. The server writes each request itself, by kind of thing, from the plan (description, requirements, sizes, views, the place of the thing's first shot), with the film's own approved footage pictures and drawings as its inputs. Send it (`vw visuals round --file out/reference-round.json`): the server names every faulty row at once; then do what its answer says. Every person gets a set; an animal gets none. The server writes a person's set from the plan (description, outfits, the place of their first shot, your added words, one line against every other person), and from the person's photo when the permission is recorded, as three separate pictures: full length from the front, the plan's first view (else full length from the side), the face. A thing's three pictures are the views the plan names (`required_views`), filled to three by its kind and never two alike: an object whole, as the film uses it, and its telling detail (the thing stays the subject; in use, the person who wears, holds or uses it as far as the use needs; on a documentary-explainer film no person, only the hand that holds it and the material the description names); a material as a surface, as the film uses it, and very close; a place as one picture, the whole place (a round posted before 17 Nov 2026 keeps its three: whole, from the other side, its fixed things); a way of working as the action or the change at its key moment, its result, and close on where it happens (hands and a tool allowed where the description names them, never required; no face); a default view that a view of the plan already shows is left out; lettering only where the description names it; every person the words act with is an element (the check warns of one missing).
Every answer of the round says what comes next (`then`): do that and add nothing of your own. `vw visuals status --wait 900` while sets are made. When they are back, look at them before the operator does: `vw visuals round --looks` lists them and fetches their pictures (work/visuals/sets/); its `how` gives the points to judge by (against the footage picture, the approved drawing, the plan's words and the operator's) and the shape of the file; the thing's kept footage pictures come with the set to compare with, also when it was not made from them (never beside a stand-in); each look turns the image model's notes into two plain lines, `chose` (what the model chose) and `aside` (what it set aside), which the operator reads in place of the notes; each picture comes with its check list (`lines`), and no model checks a set, the check is yours: answer every line of every picture, pass or fail, from what you see in the picture, never from the request or the notes, with one plain sentence for a fail; check a fact of the drawing against the drawing sheet given with the set; never pass a line you did not look at; a picture you could not open is `not_checked`, with why; with more than five sets start `vw-set-look` helpers, about five sets each, each given a group name, its element ids, the run folder's path and the tool's command line; each look is recorded with `vw visuals round --looks <file>`. The server shows the operator no set before its look. Ask nothing per element and generate nothing meanwhile. Step 1: each thing gets one answer: use its footage picture as the reference (no AI set, and the first picture in view order is its golden picture), have a clean set made from it, have a set made, or no reference needed; one footage picture can be marked not this one. Done approves the frames and orders the first three sets only, made to check the method; the others are made in one go on the operator's word, once they have judged the first; with three sets or fewer all are made at once. The server says this to the operator in its own sentence when step 1 is recorded and again when the others are ordered (`then`): pass it on as it is. The operator's word for the others is needed only when a first set did not pass: when your look says "use" for every first set, the server orders the others itself as it records the looks, with no question to the operator, and its answer says so (`then`); when a first set is not passed, could not be made or could not be checked, the others wait for the operator's word and that set is shown first, with your look's words. A set is three separate pictures, one per turn of one conversation, made from the film's own approved footage pictures and drawings where it has them (the request says the order once, the earlier winning: the operator's words, your added words, the film's own pictures (the approved drawing for shape and size, the footage picture for look, colour and wear), the plan's description, then web photographs), else from real photographs with Google Search and Image Search on; a place is one picture. The server records whether the picture model searched and shows it on the set's line: searched (with the pages, where it gave any), did not search, not asked (a person's set), or not known; never say it yourself and never guess it. The older rules for a prompt you write do not read a set's request: the wording rules read only the words you or the operator added, and the quoted-words rule, "the plan cites the footage", "measure it first" and the "Not this" list are not applied to a set. Step 2, when the sets are back and looked at: the operator judges each: Approve (choosing the reference picture of a thing, from which pictures of it start; a person's is the full-length front, with the face), Minor corrections with their words, or Make again; one click orders the other sets. A correction stays on that set; where the operator ticks "This applies to every picture of this thing" (in the chat: "Correct every picture of it"), the server keeps it for the thing, carries it into every later request of it (a later set, a still, a start picture), the later correction winning, and shows it on the thing's line: never write a correction into the plan's description. After Make again or Minor corrections nothing is made until you rewrite that request from their words, your check and your look: out/round-rewrites.json, rows {element_id, prompt}, sent with `vw visuals round --rewrite out/round-rewrites.json`. The same words are refused, the earlier request is kept, a rejected picture is never an input, and a set is made three times at most, a make that returned no picture not counted. The operator answers both steps on the page (`vw visuals page`), each in one visit. Step 1 shows one thing at a time beside the list of things, each with your proposal, its reason, the plan's description and the shots that use it, in five groups in this order: the routine things, which they may look at and accept together in one click that says how many sets are made first and that the others are asked after (never a doubtful thing, never a real person's likeness); the things with footage pictures; the things with no picture for which a set is suggested; those for which no reference is suggested; and the people the footage does not show, who need no answer: each gets a set from the description at done, and may be given words or their own photo. The buttons follow the case of the thing: Approve, Make a set, Make a set with words (their words), Upload my own, No reference needed. Each footage picture is shown with what you saw and a Keep tick: an unticked picture is only not used, and no other is searched ("Not this picture" is its own button: the next best is then shown and the thing comes back once); a ticked closest picture is taken as the thing's own; "No reference needed" names the shots made without a reference. Step 2 shows one set at a time beside the list, in four groups in this order: to judge (those you would make again or are unsure of first), could not be made, waiting to be made, settled; each set with the film's own pictures to compare, your check, your look and your two lines on the image model's notes. Its answers are Approve, Minor corrections, Make again, Upload my own and, on a set that could not be made or was made three times, Go on without a reference; a set made three times offers no remake. The first sets are judged before the others are ordered, on one button; "Do not make this set" on the waiting sets shows which shots lose a reference, never covers a person, and makes the others on the same word; a set made again shows the set before and the operator's words. Where the film's limit has no room the line says so with no amount: only the owner raises it. Run `vw visuals page` again whenever the answer says so. No cost is shown or named at the references, on the page, in the chat or in a reason you write (the owner's decision of 17 Nov 2026): the server keeps the film's limit and records every spend, and a refusal after done says the limit with no figure; never add a price or a cost word yourself. The click, then their done, is their word. In the chat (`vw visuals next`, section E), only where the page cannot be shown: the same lines in the same order with the same words, asked in turn (a person the footage does not show is not asked: the first question says how many get a set); a picture is answered there with its own button too. `vw visuals round --verdicts out/round-verdicts.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: approve|clean|ignore, words}}), `vw visuals round --sets out/round-sets.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: yes|no|correct, words, golden}}), `vw visuals round --rest --quote` (the other sets) and `vw visuals round --make E --quote` (one set that was not made) only record answers the operator has already given in their own words: never use them to answer for the operator, and nothing is ordered without their words. Refused by name on such a film: the Google Images search, the picks, nothing-fits, the separate golden call; a round answer without `kept` is an older film's and keeps them (search keywords: two to twelve words, the thing and its place or trade): follow the tool's answers. Meanwhile, for accepted gaps only and without generating or spending, draft the answer forms of every diagram, chart and title card, the drawing and material specs (the client's material and the plan; measures and web figures after the round) and the drawn layouts; nothing new on the page and no question until the round closes, then the drafts' questions as one list; update drafts the round changed. The operator gives their own picture on the page (Upload my own, on the thing's line; a person's photo with their words that they have the permission), or in the chat with `vw visuals own`. Done on step 1 is not undone (the first sets are ordered then; the others only on the operator's word): at step 2 a set is made again from the request you rewrite with the operator's words, and for one that was not made the operator may go on without a reference. The round file sent again after step 1 orders nothing and brings back only a thing that is new in the plan or whose entry in the plan changed; a thing the operator said needs no reference comes back only when they ask for it by name (`vw visuals round --back E`), as an open line. A set is never made with `vw visuals image --kind sheet` on such a film: the server refuses it. A round whose answer has no `v` is an older round: follow the tool's answers. Then part-later.md, sections 5 and 9.

parts.name: later
parts.title: The later steps (references, sheets and golden pictures; shot pictures and videos; checks; review and record; brand)
parts.text:
5. GENERATED REFERENCES, SHEETS AND GOLDEN PICTURES
Name the shot a composed picture is for (`--shot S`): its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked on the picture, with two practice lines on every scene picture (a plausible setting and scale; tools handled as a practitioner would).

When the other still is approved the next-step line says the comparison is due: give a checker that rule with both frames and send its verdict with the same round; a fail is a failed must of this drawing. It is closed only when the other drawing leaves the plan. Then a fresh `vw-motion-check` helper per shot with the round number, and `vw motion verdict --shot S --file work/motion/S/check-N.json`: the server holds the rules of rules.md sent with the upload, and a verdict answers every one of them by its words (a failed rule with `where`), or it is refused. A verdict is refused too when the brief changed after the rules were written (a font, the palette, a size): the refusal names the changed line; read the rules of that drawing again against the new brief, then upload again with them. Each rule is a must or a should (rules.md marks it). Only a failed must sends the drawing back: the failed musts go to a new `vw-motion-shot` helper, with the failed shoulds as notes to fix in the same redo. A verdict with no failed must is clean ("Passed, N notes"); the notes are shown with the drawing. A rule the checker answers "not seen" is neither a pass nor a fail: take the frames the verdict asks for, give them to the same checker for those rules only, and send its verdict with the same round number; nothing is rebuilt. A rule that does not apply to this drawing is answered "na" with `why`: it is recorded once as a note, and nothing is fetched or rebuilt for it. In round 2 or 3, give the checker the rules that failed before and the builder's list of what it changed: it answers those rules and the rules about what the fix touched, and a rule it leaves out keeps its pass. The server writes that list: from round 2, `vw motion upload` saves work/motion/S/rules-round.md, the rules the round before left failed or not seen, and the checker reads it in place of rules.md; when the brief changed since, there is no such file and every rule is answered again. Below those rules the file lists the musts that passed before: the checker answers one of them only when this upload broke it, and a fail there is a failed must. A label of this shot only that the check finds on screen too short is a must too. At most two redo rounds caused by a must. A drawing with a must still open after round 3 is held: render it (`vw motion render --shot S`) and the chat asks the operator with its card (`vw visuals next`): select it anyway (one click, recorded as selected against the check), reject it (rebuilt from round 1), or "One more round", allowed once (the server then takes round 4; after it the card offers the first two). A clean verdict (no failed must, nothing not seen) binds: the server binds the project that passed to its shot, and nothing goes in the plan (the labels and cues are there from the start; never the corner note: the server draws it in the lower right corner of every frame). Then `vw motion render --shot S --wait` (free; it checks the timing; `--wait` returns when the render is ready, as a check and a snapshot do). A later upload of the shot is bound only by its own clean verdict. It is selected like a take; a drawing without a clean verdict of its project is held. A correction the operator makes that holds for the subject: `vw motion rule --subject … --add "…" --quote "…"`. The shared look: before the first `vw motion brief` of the film's drawn graphics, read every approved spec together and record the choices that hold for every drawing, one line each, with `vw motion note --shot all --text "…"`: how each repeating part is shown, the view, the film's motions (its style's named motions and the extra ones the specs need), and which diagrams return (withdrawn with `vw motion note --shot all --remove "<the line>"`). State there the count of each shape that repeats across the drawings (how many of a part, how many divisions), so every drawing shows the same number. Every brief carries them under "Shared look (every drawing of this film)", for every builder and checker. A choice with no fact in it is yours, and you log it (`vw log`); a choice that changes a fact or a proportion is asked once, with the others, before the first drawing is built, each with your recommended answer. Nothing known beforehand is asked one at a time during the builds. A question nobody could foresee, met in the middle of a build, is asked at once: record it (`vw visuals ask`, your recommended answer first among the choices) and run `vw visuals next`; questions that wait together are asked one after the other with no build between them, and the builds that do not depend on the answer go on. The motions are binding: a builder uses the film's named motions and no others and names them in REVIEW.md. Read each REVIEW.md: a drawing that used another motion with no reason from its brief's own lines goes back once to a new `vw-motion-shot` helper with that point; never as a fact-check rule, and never a second time. The shared parts: when the film has two or more drawn graphics, after the shared look and before any brief, `vw motion parts` writes work/motion/parts/brief.md (the things two or more drawings show, then every drawn shot's brief) with the pictures to look at; one `vw-motion-parts` helper draws each repeating part once, as an SVG symbol, in work/motion/parts/parts.svg; upload it with `vw motion parts --file work/motion/parts/parts.svg`. The parts are every shape two or more drawings show, not only the things of the plan: the helper lists them first from all the specs, with their counts, and names on each part the drawings that show it; with no repeating shape it writes an empty file and there are no shared parts. The server draws one picture of the parts and the chat asks the operator: Approve, or Reject with their words, which go to a new `vw-motion-parts` helper; the next upload is asked again. `vw motion brief` is refused until the parts are approved; each brief then names the parts to use and saves parts.svg beside it, the server puts them in every drawing's page, and an upload that draws its own copy of a part it should use is refused. A parts file changed after the approval is approved again; a drawing that uses a changed part is rendered again, not rebuilt: its brief changed, so its rules are read again and the same project is uploaded and checked again before `vw motion render`. With one drawn graphic there are no shared parts. The still end-frame: every drawn shot is built first as a still, the picture as it stands at the end of the shot with no motion (a project of the shot's length that shows the end state from the first frame; on a shot whose camera moves, the end framing), uploaded with `vw motion upload --shot S --still`. Snapshot its last frame and give it to a fresh `vw-motion-check` helper, which answers only the must rules a still can show (not the rules about motion or timing); send its verdict with `vw motion verdict` as for any project. When the upload says that no rule of the drawing is one a still can show, no checker is needed: send a verdict with an empty rule list. A verdict with no failed must brings the still to the operator in the chat: the picture with Approve and Reject (the stills of one diagram in one card, in order, when they are ready together); Reject comes with their words, which go to a new `vw-motion-shot` helper to redo the still. Only after the approval is the animated project uploaded (an upload without --still is refused before), and the builder adds the motion without changing what the still shows. The still's rounds do not count against the animation's three. When the shared parts change after a still was approved, the still is uploaded, snapshotted and checked again; its approval stays when the picture is the same. While step 6 is made: order the still pictures at the start of the step, all of them in one call (`vw visuals image --file out/images.json`), at the same time as the drawn graphics are begun: one `vw-still-prompts` helper, started beside the parts helper, writes that file, one row per still, every field as text (`[{"element": "E1", "shot": "S1", "kind": "keyframe", "name": "still-S1", "prompt": "…"}]`); they need nothing from the drawings (a still another picture is made from is asked early: order the picture made from it; the server then puts the still on a chat card, and its approval also allows it as the parent), and the tool's next-step line counts the still shots with no picture asked for yet. Render each drawn graphic as soon as its verdict is clean; never wait for the others. `vw visuals next` (when nothing waits for an answer) and `vw visuals status` give a line of counts ("Drawn graphics: 5 made and checked, 3 being redone, 1 held (needs a decision). Stills: 9 made and checked."): say it to the operator each time it changes, as it is, and ask nothing with it. A drawn graphic whose render is ready comes once in `vw visuals next` to show with its one line; it asks nothing: the operator judges it on the page with the others. Nothing of step 6 is put on the page one by one: the page opens when every still, graphic in steps, component and drawn graphic is made and checked (one that could not be made is listed as such) and every held drawing is answered; until then `vw visuals page` answers with the line of counts, and nothing is published.

stages.name: assembly
steps: First the editor's package (design/115, design/132): once every gap is recorded, `vw delivery bundle` (the narration, the camera cuts by name and time, the raw AI files, the timeline, the EDL, the captions, the cut list and the relink list). The server refuses the assembly without it, and again after a gap is recorded anew: run it again. On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, `vw delivery check`, `vw delivery download` (no camera copies by default), then `vw delivery open --originals "<folder>"` on Resolve Studio. Then the assembly below, the proof copy.

`vw assembly prepare`: it lists every gap fill on one line (slot frames, what the take or asset covers, the default: trim from frame 0, or hold the last frame when the take is short; issues such as untagged colour or rotation) and the shots the logs flagged as shaky.

Show the operator that table and ask once: any fill to change (start offset, trim or hold), any flagged shot to stabilise with FFmpeg (counted in the zoom cap), and for each fill with an issue whether to use it as it is or swap it in visuals. Record only the exceptions: `vw assembly choose --shot S --offset f --end trim|hold_last [--accept-as-is]`, or several in out/fills.json with `--file out/fills.json`; `vw assembly stabilize --sub X --choice ffmpeg`. The defaults need no command.

`vw assembly build`, `vw assembly render` (A1 narration with one measured gain, A2 nat sound at the blueprint band, a -3 dBTP ceiling on the mix, no music), `vw assembly status --wait 900` until the film is ready, `vw assembly fetch` (it prints the loudness against the targets). The operator watches AND listens.

On their yes (it must say watched and listened): `vw assembly record --quote "<their words>"` records the review and the output together. On changes: `vw assembly review --decision changes --notes "…" [--frame-note mm:ss:note] --quote "…"`, change the choices the notes name, build and render again (only the changed fills are re-encoded). On a no: `--decision rejected` and `vw revise --stage visuals` or `--stage master` as the notes say.

stages.name: delivery
steps: `vw delivery bundle` again writes the full package with the approved film (approved film, narration, originals used, normalised fills, plans, SRT, finishing checklist, media-pool CSV, OPEN-EDIT).

On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, then `vw delivery check` (is Resolve installed, Studio or free, which version, enough disk; the download does not start without it), `vw delivery download` (the whole edit into runs/<code>/edit/, three files at a time, then counted and cross-checked: every file's size and fingerprint, the voiceover byte-identical, every cut pointing at a present file, the timeline's length and cut count equal to the film; the timeline is then written with this computer's paths), `vw delivery open` (free Resolve: three steps, File > Import > Timeline, then the operator plays the start, the middle and the end next to Approved-film.mp4; on their yes `vw delivery confirm --quote "<their words>"`; Resolve Studio, running with external scripting on: `vw delivery open` imports the timeline, exports .drp and .drt into Timeline/ and reads it back at 0 frames), then `vw delivery zip` for the editor. When the camera files are copies, before the handover: `vw delivery relink-check --originals "<folder>"` compares each original with Relink-list.csv and says per file: relinks as is, renamed (the relinked timeline points at the real name), a corrected timeline written (timecode), line up by hand (cuts listed with frame grabs), two originals fit (the operator picks), or no original found. `vw delivery resolve --run` is replaced; never run it (design/107).

Back on the build machine: ask the five questions (watched the film, listened, read the subtitles, the timeline matched the film, package complete) and `vw delivery final --quote "<their words>"`. Then `vw close` (retention: final film and package, narration, approved visuals, records; everything else deleted).
